qualified_claims: Removing LevelDemand while leaving Basin storage change free eliminates the low_storage_factor collapse: alpha is 1 and both managed demands are fully allocated by drawing accepted Basin storage.
Imposing only the preregistered diagnostic storage_change=0 constraint, still without LevelDemand, restores alpha=0 and the 32/0 allocation pattern.

The DUMMY-20H3/20H4 alpha collapse is therefore not specific to LevelDemand bookkeeping in the tested v2026.1.1 topology; a storage-preservation requirement is sufficient for lexicographic allocation to use low_storage_factor as a forecast degree of freedom.

The technical v1 failure was an injection-order failure only. The v3 repair preserved the frozen model, references and tolerances and applied the zero-storage bounds only after Ribasim refreshed allocator-owned bounds.

mathematical_contract.free_storage_case: alpha=1 permits storage draw and full 40+20 m3/day UserDemand allocation.
mathematical_contract.zero_storage_case: With storage_change=0 and priority-2 root demand ahead of priority-3 external demand, alpha=0 permits the 32 m3/day source to remain available to root demand.

boundaries: The hard storage_change=0 intervention is diagnostic only.
No claim that every LevelDemand configuration is equivalent to a hard zero-storage constraint.
No production prescription or production-source admission.
The result is qualified only for the tested Ribasim v2026.1.1 topology, priorities and forcing.
downstream: Release prospectively frozen DUMMY-20H6 to test accepted-storage memory versus current River-forcing forecast separation at the next allocation boundary.
